questions.stem: The United Nations was established in 1945. Where is its headquarters located?
questions.explanation: The UN was established on 24 October 1945 (after 50 founding members ratified the Charter). HQ is in New York City (extraterritorial status — not under US jurisdiction). Other major UN centres: Geneva (UNHCR, WHO, ILO, UNCTAD, WIPO, WTO), Vienna (IAEA, UNIDO, UNODC), Nairobi (UNEP, UN-Habitat), The Hague (ICJ + ICC separate from UN). Six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council (5 P + 10 non-P), Economic & Social Council, Trusteeship (suspended 1994), Secretariat, ICJ. India is a founding member; never permanent SC member (aspires to reform).

questions.stem: Match HQ to organisation: (I) Geneva (II) Washington DC (III) Paris (IV) Rome

options.option_text: (I) WHO (II) IMF & World Bank (III) UNESCO (IV) FAO

questions.explanation: GENEVA: WHO, ILO, WTO, UNHCR, UNCTAD, WIPO, ITU. NEW YORK: UN HQ, UNICEF, UNDP, UN Women, UNFPA. WASHINGTON DC: IMF, World Bank, IFC. PARIS: UNESCO, OECD. ROME: FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization), WFP (World Food Programme), IFAD. VIENNA: IAEA, UNIDO, UNODC, OPEC. NAIROBI: UNEP, UN-Habitat. THE HAGUE: ICJ (UN's judicial organ), ICC (independent). BRUSSELS: EU, NATO. BASEL: BIS. Memorise the top-20 HQ-org mappings — very high-hit-rate on exams.

questions.stem: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The ICJ — principal judicial organ of the UN — is headquartered at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. The ONLY principal UN organ NOT in New York. Succeeded the Permanent Court of International Justice (1920). 15 judges, 9-year terms. India's Justice Dalveer Bhandari (elected 2012, re-elected 2017 till 2027). Other courts at The Hague: INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT (ICC — 2002, for individuals; not a UN body), Permanent Court of Arbitration (1899). Geneva has WTO Dispute Settlement (not a court).

questions.stem: OPEC (Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded in 1960 at the Baghdad Conference (Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela — the 5 founders). HQ initially in Geneva (1960-65), moved to VIENNA in 1965 (where it remains). Current members: 12 (after Qatar left 2019, Ecuador 2020, Angola 2023). Most recent: Equatorial Guinea, Congo, Gabon joined. OPEC+ refers to OPEC plus 10 non-OPEC (led by Russia) that cooperates on output. OPEC controls ~40% of global oil production and ~80% of proven reserves. Saudi Arabia is the de facto leader. Meetings in Vienna twice yearly.

questions.stem: Which Indian city hosts the headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), launched by India and France in 2015?
questions.explanation: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) is headquartered at GURUGRAM, Haryana — India's first treaty-based international intergovernmental organisation. Launched at COP21 Paris 2015 by PM Modi & President Hollande. Treaty entered force 2017. HQ inaugurated by PM Modi & UN SG Antonio Guterres in 2018. Target: 1 TW of solar capacity by 2030 and mobilise $1 trillion investment. Originally open only to countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn; expanded in 2020 to all UN member states. 119 members and signatories. DG: Ajay Mathur (till 2024), succeeded by Dr. B.N. Satpathy.

questions.stem: The BRICS grouping, formed in 2009 (BRIC) and expanded to BRICS with South Africa's entry in 2010, was further expanded in January 2024 with which new members?

options.option_text: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE (4 new members)

questions.explanation: Original BRIC (2009): Brazil, Russia, India, China. South Africa joined 2010 → BRICS. At the 15th Summit (Johannesburg, Aug 2023), BRICS invited Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE — to join from 1 Jan 2024. Argentina DECLINED (after Milei came to power). Saudi Arabia's status is 'invited but deferred'. So effective Jan 2024: 9 members — Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE. Indonesia formally joined Jan 2025 as the 10th member. HQ: New Development Bank in Shanghai; Contingent Reserve Arrangement. India's 16th BRICS summit hosted at Kazan, Russia, Oct 2024.

questions.stem: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established in 1995, replacing which earlier agreement?

options.option_text: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)

questions.explanation: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 following the Marrakesh Agreement (1994) that concluded the Uruguay Round of GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947) negotiations. WTO REPLACES GATT as a formal institution but retains GATT as one of its covered agreements (for goods). Other WTO covered agreements: GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property), DSU (dispute settlement understanding). HQ: Geneva. Current DG: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria — first woman and first African, appointed March 2021). 164 members. India has been challenging many WTO decisions on agricultural subsidies, digital trade, MSP. The 'Appellate Body' is currently dysfunctional due to US blocking new appointments since 2019.

questions.stem: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established 1966; HQ at MANILA, Philippines. 68 member economies (49 from Asia-Pacific + 19 from outside). Current President: Masatsugu Asakawa (Japan, since 2020 — all ADB Presidents since founding have been Japanese). Largest ADB-funded countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh. In contrast: AIIB (Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, 2016) — HQ at BEIJING, China; President Jin Liqun (Chinese). India is ADB's 4th-largest shareholder but a NON-FOUNDING member of AIIB (joined as 2nd-largest shareholder). NDB (New Development Bank / BRICS Bank) — HQ at SHANGHAI, first President KV Kamath (India, 2015-20).

questions.stem: SAARC has how many member countries and where is its secretariat located?
questions.explanation: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 with 7 members. Afghanistan joined 2007 as 8th member. Current members (8): Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka. HQ: Kathmandu, Nepal. Current Secretary-General: Golam Sarwar (Bangladesh, from March 2023). Observer states: Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, Myanmar, S. Korea, US, Mauritius. SAARC summits have been stalled since the 18th (Kathmandu 2014); 19th scheduled Islamabad 2016 was boycotted by India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Afghanistan after Uri attack. Effective successor: BIMSTEC (since 1997) — includes Bay of Bengal countries, HQ Dhaka.
